- If CI starts automatically and later becomes stale because a finding that must be fixed on a real input requires another candidate revision, stop treating that run as a gate. Cancel it only when a supported authorized interface permits cancellation.

### Review findings on real inputs

These rules govern every review finding on the pull request, from the automated code review or from a person.

- Real input. A finding's triggering input is real when it exists on `main` or in an approved work unit's planned deliverable; occurs in the product's real operating environment, such as the deployed services, the hosted CI runner, the operator's shell or the vendor's responses; or can be supplied by a user, a vendor or an attacker through an interface the product exposes. An input constructed only to exercise code justifies no requirement, design element, test, fix or blocking finding; an input outside the real set receives one refusal or a stated limit, never a model of it.
- Findings below P1. A finding is fixed when it shows a wrong result, a crash or a guarantee breach on a real input. Otherwise, the reply on the thread gives the traced path and the stated limit, and the thread is resolved. Declining a security finding goes to the Product Owner first. A blanket instruction to fix every finding on a pull request is read under this rule. The standing default is to fix only a wrong result on a real input, or a breach of a read-only or no-secrets guarantee; a snapshot-precision finding is a hypothetical-input finding unless it shows a write that the tool itself, or code it runs in the checkout, can make.
- P1 findings. A P1 finding is a review finding labelled P1 or any higher priority, such as P0; the priority is the label the reviewer gives. A P1 finding whose triggering input is real is fixed. It is not declined, deferred to a later change, recorded as a stated limit, or resolved on cost, effort, design preference, a plan's earlier choice, an ADR's stated limit or a "not worth its code" judgement. Fixed means that the wrong result, crash or guarantee breach the finding reports no longer occurs on that real input, shown by a test that fails without the fix; a typed refusal of the input is a fix when refusing it is correct behavior for the product. The thread stays open until the fix is pushed and the finding's own check of it is answered. A pull request with an open P1 thread on a real input is not merge-ready.
- The one P1 exception. A P1 finding may be declined only when its triggering input is not real, so that the input is one constructed only to exercise the code. The reply on the thread gives the traced path and shows why the input can never occur in the product. Declining a P1 goes to the Product Owner first, and the thread is resolved only after that.
- Repeated finding class. When two consecutive review rounds on one pull request raise findings of the same class, meaning the same component or contract, stop fixing instances and ask the Product Owner one design question: narrow the design, accept a stated limit, or rescope. For a P1 on a real input, accepting a stated limit is not an option: the answer is a fix, a narrowed design that removes the wrong result (a typed refusal included), or a rescope through the native route, and the P1 is resolved before the pull request merges. This is a design trigger by finding class. It is not a push count, a pause threshold or a CI-budget control. Ask the question in the PR-35 session and continue there on the answer: work a narrowed design or a stated limit in that session, and take a rescope through the formal rescope route.
- Unchanged duty. Nothing in these rules weakens the existing duty to fix a real defect at any priority.

ops.new:
## Finding on a constructed input

Given a review finding below P1 whose triggering input exists nowhere on `main`, in an approved deliverable, in the product's real operating environment or behind an interface the product exposes, PR-35 replies on the thread with the traced path and the stated limit and resolves the thread. It writes no fix, test or model of that input. A security finding declined this way goes to the Product Owner first.

## Real-input P1

Given a P1 finding whose triggering input is real, PR-35 fixes it, with a test that fails without the fix, and keeps the thread open until the fix is pushed and the finding's own check of it is answered. It never records a stated limit for it or declines it on cost, effort or design preference, and it does not return `MERGE_PENDING` while that thread is open. Only a P1 whose input is not real may be declined, Product Owner first.

## Repeated finding class

Given two consecutive review rounds on one pull request that raise findings of the same component or contract, PR-35 stops fixing instances and asks the Product Owner one design question in its own session: narrow the design, accept a stated limit, or rescope. It continues on the answer. For a P1 on a real input the answer is a fix, a narrowed design or a rescope, never a stated limit. Push count, review-round count and CI spend are not triggers.

## Pull request subscription

# PART-13 (MODIFICATION-20261027-gcfpe-backlog-open-items): an added successor row has no historical row;
        # it must sit immediately after its anchor row, and every other row keeps its historical neighbours.
        all_ids = [row.get("id") for row in rows]
        ids = [row_id for row_id in all_ids if row_id not in SUCCESSOR_ADDED_ROWS]
        history_ids = [row.get("id") for row in history_rows]
        position_findings = 0
        for added, anchor in SUCCESSOR_ADDED_ROWS.items():
            if (added in history_ids or all_ids.count(added) != 1 or anchor not in all_ids
                    or all_ids.index(added) != all_ids.index(anchor) + 1):
                position_findings += 1
                results.append(finding(
                    "FMV-ORACLE-019", str(oracle_path),
                    f"row={added}; an added successor row must occur once, immediately after {anchor}, "
                    f"and have no historical row",
